A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WildChat-AQA benchmark and PROBE retrieval method. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations and ablations in Tables 3–7, plus human annotation agreement in Table 2.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds textual-similarity baseline scores and more detailed token-cost measurements.

M1.justification: PROBE retains broad query generation, metadata filtering, max-pooling of retrieval scores and top-k evidence selection. Algorithm 1 and the construction procedures and prompts in Appendix E remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 182,330 conversations and 6,027 questions. Appendix B retains the question categories, language counts and topic taxonomy. Figure 2's illustrative language changes from Russian to German, but both languages were already represented.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds BM25 and Cosine Sim as direct candidate-ranking baselines without conversation context. BM25 already appeared in retrieval comparisons, but its participation in this direct-ranking comparison is new. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: Table 5 adds input-token cost to the existing recall/NDCG@5 evaluation. The ten-candidate ranking protocol, NDCG cutoffs and stratified 10% ablation subset remain unchanged. Appendix D's new chunking description does not establish that an existing experimental setting changed.

E4.justification: Table 5 extends the context-size analysis with token costs across 5–500 conversations. Existing query/filter ablations, oracle-context comparisons and reasoning-mode tests remain. v2 also mentions human keyword validation, but provides no separate results or sampling protocol.

E5.justification: The agreement reporting and Appendix E.8's Monte Carlo standard-deviation estimate and 90% confidence threshold are retained. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals for benchmark scores or new significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds NDCG@1 scores of 0.2320 for BM25 and 0.2761 for Cosine Sim. Table 5 adds token counts, including 15.4M, 11.3M and 6.31M for RAG, PROBE and Oracle at 500 summarized conversations. Existing performance and agreement scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The PROBE formulation, taxonomy-quality definitions in Equations 1–3, keyword-equivalence rules and question-filtering threshold in Equation 4 remain mathematically unchanged. No new theorem, proof or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: aggregative question answering, WildChat-AQA, PROBE and evidence that existing approaches face reasoning and computational-cost limitations.

C2.justification: v2 narrows the negative finetuning interpretation to the tested direct-training setup. It expands limitations from artificial question phrasing to artifact overfitting and uncertain generalization to human-authored questions, and adds discussion of keyword annotation noise and demographic profiling.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly specifies raw-conversation chunks of at most 512 tokens, overlap up to 128 tokens and no chunking for summaries. v2 also updates repository and visualization addresses and clarifies construction and finetuning descriptions; these disclosures do not demonstrate changed runs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Valdez et al. (2020), on longitudinal social-media analysis, to support the introduction's societal-insights motivation. Appendix A's related-work coverage and the positioning against QA, summarization, RAG and text-to-SQL remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main text receives wording and tense edits, Section 2 is renamed from WildChat-AQA to Aggregative Question Answering, explanations are expanded and acknowledgements are added. The overall section sequence and appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with an explicit filter/summarize/aggregate illustration; Figure 2's labels and example are revised. Tables 3 and 5 gain rows and a column, respectively. Plots receive sizing, placement and tick adjustments, while appendix tables and prompts are reflowed.

improvement.justification: Additional baselines, token-cost breakdowns, chunking details and more qualified interpretations modestly strengthen evaluation transparency and reproducibility. The core evidence remains stable. These gains are tempered by an undocumented claim of human keyword validation and imprecise 'no better than random' wording despite Cosine Sim exceeding random in Table 3.
